\title{Population exposure to mmWave massive-MIMO across cities:\\
a deterministic ray-traced spine}
\author{AEGIS study report}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We compute the distribution of radio-frequency exposure across a walking
pedestrian population under a \SI{28}{\giga\hertz} massive-MIMO deployment, for
real cities of differing urban morphology. Pedestrians follow real walking
routes (Google Directions); the base stations sit on real building rooftops.
Exposure is evaluated coherently:
each base-station sector forms a fixed maximum-ratio-transmission beam toward its
served users, and every bystander body absorbs power according to the coherent
body-surface channel, $S_\mathrm{ab}(\mathbf r) = \lVert \tilde{\mathbf
G}(\mathbf r)\,\mathbf x \rVert^2$. The macro channel is deterministic: rays are
traced through the actual city mesh (buildings, ground, materials) with
diffraction. This report presents the per-city population exposure CDFs, the
headline deliverable, and serves as the deterministic reference against which a
stochastic 3GPP TR~38.901 channel will later be compared.
\end{abstract}

\section{Method}

\subsection{Pipeline}
For each city we build a triangle mesh from OpenStreetMap within a fixed radius
of the centre (building footprints and heights, a ground plane, tag-based
materials), and export it once to a Mitsuba scene for ray tracing. A repulsive
(minimum-spacing) point process thins rooftop candidates to a site set. Each site
carries three \(8\times8\) sector panels, each covering a \(\pm\SI{60}{\degree}\)
azimuth wedge out to a finite mmWave range. A synchronised pedestrian crowd walks
across the core; a body is illuminated only by sectors whose wedge and range it
falls inside.

\subsection{Coherent dosimetry}
Each sector beams toward its served users with a fixed MRT precoder \(\mathbf x\)
built from the served user's ray-traced channel. The per-element body-surface
channel \(\tilde{\mathbf G}(\mathbf r)\) carries phase and polarisation, and the
per-person scalar exposure is \(\mathbf x^{H} \mathbf Q\, \mathbf x\), where the
exposure operator \(\mathbf Q = \sum_m a_m\, \tilde{\mathbf G}[m]^{H}
\tilde{\mathbf G}[m]\) sums over body triangles. As a body translates between
ray-trace updates, \(\mathbf Q\) is refreshed analytically by the translation
phasor rather than re-traced.

\subsection{Determinism and the ray tracer}
The deterministic arm traces the actual city mesh, so occlusion and multipath are
geometric, not statistical. Diffraction is enabled (it roughly doubles the
captured power at near-ground receivers in dense cores by finding rooftop-edge
paths). The shoot-and-bounce sample count is set near its convergence plateau.

\subsection{Cost reductions for breadth}
To run several cities, fidelity knobs are dialled down deliberately
(Section~\ref{sec:knobs}); the pipeline supports raising every one of them. The
per-person scalar \(\mathbf x^H \mathbf Q\, \mathbf x\) is the reported metric;
the expensive per-triangle peak-\(S_\mathrm{ab}\) map (for an ICNIRP-fraction
figure) is left off this pass. The center-path set is capped to the strongest few
by power, which preserves the absorbed power to better than \SI{0.4}{\percent}
while bounding the exposure-operator cost.

Figure~\ref{fig:cdf} is the headline result: the population exposure
distribution for each city, computed end to end through the deterministic
pipeline. The spread across cities reflects morphology, site density, and the
line-of-sight fraction the ray tracer resolves.

\section{Knobs dialled down for this pass}
\label{sec:knobs}
This pass trades fidelity for breadth. Each knob is a config
knob and can be raised:
\begin{itemize}
  \item crowd size per city (modest, not yet CDF-converged),
  \item deployment realisations \(K=1\) (no marginalisation band yet),
  \item center paths capped to the strongest few by power,
  \item the per-triangle peak-\(S_\mathrm{ab}\) map omitted (scalar exposure only),
  \item a single static phantom pose per body.
\end{itemize}

\section{Next}
The stochastic 3GPP TR~38.901 coherent channel (geometry-blind, a
\(P_\mathrm{LOS}(d)\)-weighted LOS/NLOS blend) will be evaluated on the same
crowd and deployment, so the paired, scale-invariant deterministic-vs-stochastic
agreement can be reported. The cross-city spread will be explained with
covariates (site density, footprint density, LOS fraction) rather than a grand
mean.
